seo.title: Service Area
seo.description: {{name}} works anywhere in Oregon within about {{driveMinutes}} minutes' drive of our {{city}} shop: the Portland metro, the north Willamette Valley, and out toward the Coast Range, the Gorge and the Cascade foothills.

hero.title: Roofing across northwest Oregon
hero.lead: Our line is a drive time, not a radius: anywhere in Oregon about {{driveMinutes}} minutes from the {{city}} shop. That takes in the Portland metro, the north Willamette Valley and the foothills on either side, out to the Gorge.

image.alt: A row of older wood-sided houses with steep, dark shingle roofs on a Portland street

hero.caption: Older Portland houses on a winter afternoon: steep gables, shingle roofs, trees close by.

line.title: How the line is drawn
line.body:
The shaded area on the map isn't a circle with a compass point in {{city}}. It's everywhere you can drive to from the shop in about {{driveMinutes}} minutes, measured over real roads without rush-hour traffic.

That's why the shape looks the way it does. It runs a long way down I-5 toward Salem and Albany, and up US-26 to Sandy and Welches, because those roads are fast. It stops well short of the coast, where the roads over the Coast Range are slow, even though the distance on a map is similar.

Why drive time

A roof is rarely one visit. There's the estimate, the job, sometimes a return trip for a flashing detail or a gutter adjustment, and a look after the first big storm. Keeping the work within a reasonable drive means more of each day goes into your roof and less into the truck, and it means we can come back without it being an expedition.

Why it stops at the Columbia

We're licensed with Oregon's Construction Contractors Board, CCB #{{ccb}}. A CCB license covers work in Oregon. Washington licenses contractors separately, so the line follows the state line and the river, not the drive time.

You can look up any Oregon contractor's license, bond and insurance on the CCB's website. It's worth doing for anyone you hire.

directory.title: County by county
directory.intro: North to south, with the towns inside the line. Most counties are only partly in reach; the towns listed are the ones that are.

counties.Columbia: River towns on the Columbia along US-30, from Scappoose and St. Helens down to Rainier, and Vernonia up in the timber of the Nehalem valley.
counties.Washington: The shop's county. Beaverton, Hillsboro, Tigard and the Tualatin Valley, out to Forest Grove, Banks and Gaston at the foot of the Coast Range.
counties.Multnomah: Portland and the east county: Gresham and Troutdale, and Corbett up on the rim at the west end of the Gorge.
counties.Hood River: The Oregon side of the Gorge: Cascade Locks, and Hood River at the far end of the drive.
counties.Yamhill: Newberg and Dundee on 99W, McMinnville and Carlton in wine country, and Sheridan and Willamina toward the Coast Range.
counties.Clackamas: Lake Oswego and West Linn down to Oregon City, Wilsonville, Canby and Molalla, then east through Sandy and Estacada to Welches on the way to the mountain.
counties.Polk: Across the Willamette from Salem: Dallas, Monmouth and Independence.
counties.Marion: Salem, Keizer and Woodburn on the I-5 corridor, and Silverton, Mt. Angel, Stayton and Aumsville toward the Cascade foothills.
counties.Linn: The south edge of the line, down I-5: Albany and Jefferson.

weather.title: What the weather does to roofs here
weather.intro: One service area, four kinds of weather. It's all the Northwest, but a roof in Welches lives a different life from one in Tigard. In general terms, this is what each part of the area throws at a roof.

zones.title: The valley floor
zones.where: Portland, Beaverton, Hillsboro, Tigard, Newberg, McMinnville, Woodburn, Salem, Albany
zones.body: Long wet seasons rather than big storms: most of the year's rain falls between October and May, in gray weeks that never quite dry out. Roofs under firs and oaks, and north-facing slopes, stay damp all winter, and that's where moss takes hold. Summers are dry and can be hot, which ages shingles from the other side.
watch: Moss on shaded and north-facing slopes
Needles and leaves in valleys and gutters

zones.title: Coast Range foothills
zones.where: Forest Grove, Banks, Gaston, Vernonia, Sheridan, Willamina, Dallas
zones.body: More rain than the valley floor and heavier timber close to the house. Roofs sit in shade longer, collect more needles and stay wet longer after each storm, so moss grows faster. Southwest winter storms reach these towns first.
watch: Wind-driven rain at rakes and edges

zones.title: The Gorge and the east winds
zones.where: Troutdale, Corbett, Cascade Locks, Hood River
zones.body: Wind is the story. In winter, cold east wind pours out of the Gorge and hits Troutdale and Corbett hardest. When that cold air sits under a Pacific storm, rain freezes as it lands, and ice storms can reach well into Portland. Nailing, sealing and ridge caps matter more here than anywhere else in the area.

zones.title: Cascade foothills
zones.body: Higher ground, more rain and more snow, especially as you climb toward the mountain. Snow sits on roofs longer, ice dams are possible at the eaves, and dense fir means needles in every valley and gutter. Ice-and-water shield at the eaves earns its keep up here.
watch: Snow and ice at the eaves

pastTheLine.title: Just past the line? Call anyway
pastTheLine.body:
The line on the map is a guide, not a wall. If you're a few minutes outside it, in Oregon, call us. Depending on the job, we may still be able to schedule it.

What decides it is mostly the size of the work and the time of year. A full replacement or a commercial roof is worth a longer drive; a small repair far outside the line may not be, and if it isn't, we'll say so and point you toward finding someone closer.

card.label: When you call
card.intro: These help us give you a straight answer on the first call:
items: The town, or the nearest cross streets
What kind of work: repair, replacement, gutters, maintenance
A rough size, like a single-story house or a two-story with a garage
Photos, if you can take them safely from the ground

closingCta.title: Inside the line?
closingCta.body: If you're within about {{driveMinutes}} minutes of {{city}}, the estimate is free and it's written down. Tell us what you're seeing and we'll come look.
